about: How a tool that declares its options or parameters is given its arguments, and which arguments it refuses. The runners of tools (StandaloneToolRunner, GrailsApplicationContextCommandRunner) are held to these cases by ToolArgumentsSpec of grails-core, and the command line, which checks the same rules against the catalog before it starts Gradle, by a copy of this file.
tools: the declarations of each tool, exactly as its descriptor and the catalog have them (options and parameters in the shape of help --json). A tool with neither takes whatever it is given.

cases: the arguments a tool is given after its name; either refused, the <what> of the line '| Error NAME: <what>. grails help NAME shows its options', after which the tool ends with the exit code 2, or accepted: bound is what the fields of the declarations hold then, by the first long name of an option or the label of a parameter (a field that holds null is left out); remaining is what the command line of the tool says are its parameters; options, where given, is every option of the command line of the tool by its names without the hyphens.

The arguments are read from left to right, and the first that is wrong is the refusal: an option that is not declared (by its name before any '='; a name that is not one or two hyphens, a letter or digit and at most 62 letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores is said as 'an option it was given'), a value given to a switch, an option that is given again and is not repeatable, an option that needs a value and is last or is followed by '--' or by a declared option (with or without '=value'), and a value of the wrong type for an option. Then each required option that is missing, in the order they are declared; then the parameters in their order, each value of the wrong type and each required one that is missing; then the arguments more than the parameters take.

The forms: --name value, --name=value, -x value, -x=value, a switch alone, and '--', after which every argument is a parameter. An argument that does not start with '-', the argument '-' alone, and a negative number (-5, -1.5) that no option has as its name are parameters. An argument -Dname=value, with a name, is a system property of the tool's command line and is never refused. Names and choices are matched as they are written, upper and lower case apart. An integer is an optional sign and digits within the range of a long; a field of the type int takes one within the range of an int, which only the runner knows.
